summary: New entry ntḥr is proposed from two tokens, both 3sg.m Preterit in questions in one interview. Only these Preterit spellings are attested; an Infectum, Detransitive or broader paradigm is not reconstructed.

Stem I follows the provisional m-prefixed quadriliteral classification used in the reader and comparable glossary entries. The internal Arabic-derived n/t material need not be native Turoyo root morphology; final stem/root segmentation remains editorial.
Permitted nḥr lookup describes slaughtering (I nḥəlle/noḥər, III manḥalle/manḥər) and does not supply the suicide formation. Searches for məntaḥ and mənṭaḥ yielded no existing glossary collocation.

A relationship with Arabic intaḥara and with the nḥr lexical family is a plausible loan analysis, not an independently proved etymology. Retain ntḥr as the assigned proposed entry rather than silently merging it into nḥr.
An intransitive self-killing predicate with an l-agent is active here; reflexive meaning alone does not establish Detransitive morphology.
Should the editors retain ntḥr as an m-prefixed quadriliteral I entry, label it Q, or cross-file it as a borrowed derived formation under nḥr? The meaning is clear but segmentation is provisional.
Is mənṭaḥarle at Jan 2.27/4574 a conventional emphatic variant, dialect spelling or transcription? Preserve ṭ until checked.
Obtain an actual Infectum and further persons from a native speaker; no unattested base form is supplied.
Both examples are questions, so neither establishes the occurrence of a historical suicide.
